item.title: Kerby Joseph ready to roar in return to Lions: 'I'm used to being counted out'
item.description: For everyone who doubted whether he’d play football again, Kerby Joseph insists he never did. Joseph will play his first game in 406 days this Sunday, Nov. 22, when the Detroit Lions host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field. He missed the final 12 games last season with a cartilage condition in his knee and spent the first half of this season on the physically unable to perform list. Activated to the 53-man roster Wednesday, Joseph said Friday he’s ready to “crank” when he gets on the field. “I’m used to being counted out, I’m used to being doubted,” Joseph said. “It just doesn’t faze me no more. So even when it happened, I already knew I was going to be back there, even though everybody else thought I wasn’t going to be. But I already knew I was.” Joseph’s future has been a mystery since he first experienced swelling in his knee after a training camp practice last summer. He tried to play through the injury early in the season, but the Lions shut him down last October when the pain became too much to bear. He returned to practice briefly last December and said Friday the team’s decision to put him on injured reserve was the lowest point of his ordeal. “That was the first time I ever in my entire life gave up on something,” Joseph said. “Not totally gave up, but said I couldn’t go. So that was the first time ever, so I didn’t really know how to take that. But I took it with a grain of salt and then I just had a bigger chip on my shoulder ever since.” RELATED: Why Kerby Joseph still looks like a difference maker in practice Joseph bashed internet speculation his injury was career-ending – “Twitter doctors, they don’t know what I’m talking about. How you going to tell me about my body?” he said – but acknowledged Friday how meaningful it will be to play a football game again. Joseph declined to share the lengths he went to get his knee healthy this offseason, saying only, “God gave me the instruments to get back here.” “[This is] something I’ve been working hard all my life to do, and just to be back out here when the odds weren’t looking in my favor is just, man, it’s just amazing to just come out here and play with my teammates again, to play this game I love,” he said. Lions coach Dan Campbell has tried in recent weeks to temper expectations for Joseph’s return, and he did so again Friday cautioning, “there’s going to be a little rust.” “In practice there was rust when he started three weeks ago, and he’s kicked some of that off as we’ve gone here so this’ll be his first game in a minute,” Campbell said. “Don’t expect it to be perfect, but he’s a football player. And I think he’ll do some things, play within the system and be good.” Joseph said he has not experienced any knee pain since he returned to practice, and he said he expects to be the same impact player he was before his injury. “This [stuff] ain’t rusty,” he said. item.title: Nashville SC out to complete MLS Cup-Supporters' Shield history
item.description: Nashville SC out to complete MLS Cup-Supporters' Shield history By Ben Wright NASHVILLE – In Major League Soccer's 31-year history, only eight Supporters’ Shield winners have gone on to win MLS Cup presented by Audi. Nashville SC are looking to become the ninth, starting with Sunday's Round One Best-of-3 Series opener vs. FC Cincinnati (4 pm ET | Apple TV ; FS1, FOX Deportes). The Boys in Gold made history during the regular season, setting league records for points (77), wins (23), home wins (15), goals conceded (25), and fewest losses (3). Add a Concacaf Champions Cup semifinal run in the spring, and they’ve compiled one of the best seasons in recent memory. However, Nashville know that it will all ultimately feel like a disappointment if they don’t complete an MLS Cup-Supporters' Shield double by lifting the Philip F. Anschutz Trophy on Dec. 18. "We were happy to break the record. That was the goal in the end. We achieved it, and now it's almost a new season. A new tournament starts,” club captain Hany Mukhtar said on Tuesday. “We need to be very sharp and locked in to know what is on the line, but also to know that we are the best team ever, and we should have the confidence.” ⚽🏆 ALL FOR THE CUP Every match matters. Don't miss a moment of the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs. Watch on Apple TV Team of destiny? It’s hard not to look at Nashville and expect them to win it all. By virtue of winning the Shield, they’ll play all but one of their Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs matches at GEODIS Park, including MLS Cup, should they reach it. They’ve been virtually automatic at their home stadium this year, going 15W-0L-2D and outscoring their opponents 48-14. They’re leaning on their experiences winning the US Open Cup in 2025 and making a run to the 2026 Concacaf Champions Cup semifinals, in which they became the first MLS team to ever win at Mexico City’s Estadio Azteca, as tangible proof that they can deliver with everything on the line. “There is a different mindset, but we have shown, last year in Open Cup and this year in the Champions League, that we are capable of knockout situations and having the pressure a little bit on,” said Mukhtar, the 2022 Landon Donovan MLS MVP. “At the end of the day, there's nothing to fear. We have beaten all of them. We just need to do what we do best.” At the same time, Nashville know they have a target on their backs and history against them. While Shield winners rarely lift MLS Cup, there's some modern-day MLS precedent after LAFC completed the double in 2022. “We look at this as an extension of the regular season; we want to continue to do the same preparation, the same process of how we're gonna prepare for an opponent,” said head coach B.J. Callaghan. “I think this team is a team that maybe history hasn't had to always define it. Our guys are focused on understanding that the guarantee that we have is a three-game series. item.title: Chiefs make official Kenneth Walker III injury decision ahead of Week 11
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs are preparing for another important stretch of the NFL season, but they will have to do so without one of their most important offensive players. With a quick turnaround coming next week, the Chiefs have been cautious with Kenneth Walker III as he continues to deal with a groin injury. After monitoring his status throughout the week, Kansas City has made its decision regarding his availability for Week 11. MORE: 7 NFL teams with best chance to win Super Bowl LXI entering Week 11 Kenneth Walker officially ruled out against Cardinals Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III (9). Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images. Kenneth Walker III will miss another game for the Kansas City Chiefs, officially ruling him out for Sunday’s Week 11 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. The decision comes after Walker missed last week’s game against the Atlanta Falcons and was unable to return to practice throughout the week. Walker has been dealing with a groin injury, and the Chiefs have elected not to rush him back onto the field. Head coach Andy Reid indicated earlier in the week that Walker was improving but emphasized the importance of avoiding a setback. Kenneth Walker is out again for the #Chiefs, with a quick turnaround coming next week. — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 20, 2026 The decision is not particularly surprising given Walker’s status throughout the week. Kansas City has been cautious with the running back, and after missing multiple practices, there was little indication he would be ready to return for Sunday’s game. Walker will now miss his second consecutive game, leaving the Chiefs without one of their most productive offensive players. The rookie has taken advantage of his opportunities and could once again see a significant workload against Arizona. The timing of Walker’s absence is also important. Kansas City faces the Cardinals in Week 11 before a quick turnaround to a Thanksgiving night matchup against the Buffalo Bills in Week 12. item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Bears get 2 massive injury updates for Saints clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bears received encouraging injury updates on wide receiver Luther Burden III and running back Kyle Monangai ahead of Sunday’s Week 11 matchup against the New Orleans Saints . Chicago’s final injury report, released Friday, confirmed that both players have no game-day injury designation after participating fully in practice throughout the week. Burden had been dealing with a concussion, while Monangai was recovering from a toe injury. Both players were listed as full participants Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, clearing the way for their availability against New Orleans. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The updates provide a boost to the Bears’ offense as the team looks to improve its 7-2 record and maintain momentum following its bye week. Meanwhile, Monangai’s recovery represents another positive development for Chicago’s rushing attack. The running back previously missed time with a turf toe injury that initially sidelined him for the Bears’ Week 5 matchup against the Green Bay Packers . Chicago’s final injury report also revealed that defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons practiced fully Friday after being limited Wednesday and Thursday with a knee injury. However, the Bears will be without cornerback Kyler Gordon , who was ruled out with a shoulder injury after missing all three practices. Wide receiver Zavion Thomas is also questionable with an ankle injury after sitting out Friday’s practice. item.title: Mildly interesting players are being non-tendered
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - SEPTEMBER 07: Nolan Gorman #16 of the St. Louis Cardinals looks on prior to the game between the St. Louis Cardinals and the San Francisco Giants at Oracle Park on Monday, September 7, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Kavin Mistry/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The deadline for MLB teams to tender contracts to players who are on the 40 man roster but not currently under contract is 4 p.m. Central today. Players who are not tendered a contract by that time will become free agents. This provides one of the nerdy kind of exciting times in the offseason — a meatier, more substantive version of the Rule 5 Draft. We get to speculate as to what arb-eligible players may be cut loose by teams that do not want to risk the player getting a salary in arbitration in excess of what the team thinks the player is worth. We get to see what contracts are announced today, thus learning which players were in danger of being non-tendered if they didn’t agree to a contract before the deadline. And there will be a spate of players who will hit the free agent market and make us say, oh, hey, he’s a free agent, My Favorite Team should try to sign him. Usually that desire for Your Favorite Team to sign said player is dampened once you take a look at his recent performance level and/or injury history, but still, that bit of frisson when you see a name that once was associated with something of value being out there and available is something we can all enjoy in these noisome November nights. Take, for instance, Nolan Gorman. He was the Cardinals’ first round pick in 2018, taken four picks after the Rangers selected Cole Winn. Keith Law actually mocked Gorman to the Rangers in one of his mock drafts that year.* He was a consensus top-100 prospect from 2019-22, and was a consensus top-35 prospect in 2022. In 2023 he put up an 805 OPS with 27 home runs. And he’s reportedly being non-tendered. The Rangers should jump all over him! * In searching to see if I had done a draft preview of Gorman that year, I found this write-up I did in 2019 of someone named Jimmy Lewis. For the life of me, I have no memory of doing this write-up, or of this Jimmy Lewis guy ever existing. Alas, he’s kind of been bad since then. He’s played second base and third base, neither of them well, and after slashing .204/.284/.385 in the 2024-25 seasons, Gorman ended up splitting 2026 between the majors and AAA, slashing .184/.272/.308 in the former and .182/.328/.430 in the latter. So yeah, you can see how he’s ended up in the late-November second wave of free agents. Along those same lines, the Twins are reportedly non-tendering Bailey Ober and Trevor Larnach, each of whom were entering their final season of arbitration eligibility, and each of whom would seem to be in line for high-seven-figure 2027 salaries via the arbitration process. item.title: Detroit Lions Rule 1 Player OUT, 6 Questionable vs. Buccaneers
item.description: The Detroit Lions have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and there is both good news and bad news for Dan Campbell’s squad. The bad news? Detroit will once again be without starting center Cade Mays , who has officially been ruled out with an ankle injury. The good news? All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph has no injury designation after being listed as a full participant throughout the week, putting him in position to make his long-awaited return to the field. According to the Lions’ official injury report , six additional players are listed as questionable for Sunday’s game at Ford Field. With Detroit already dealing with devastating injuries on defense, the status of several key contributors will be worth monitoring before kickoff. Detroit Lions center Cade Mays (64) warms up ahead of the game between Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. The veteran center did not participate in practice Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday, leaving the Lions with little choice but to rule him out. With Mays sidelined, Juice Scruggs is expected to remain Detroit’s starting center , providing continuity for an offensive line that has been forced to make adjustments in recent weeks. Scruggs will face a challenging assignment against Tampa Bay’s defensive front, particularly when matched up against massive defensive tackle Vita Vea. The Lions had already been monitoring Mays’ status throughout the week , but Friday’s designation officially eliminates any possibility of him playing Sunday. Detroit also has a quick turnaround following the Buccaneers game, with its traditional Thanksgiving matchup against the Chicago Bears coming just four days later. For now, Mays’ availability beyond Sunday remains uncertain. item.title: Chris Russo fears entire 2027 MLB season is ‘in jeopardy’
item.description: Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports Less than three months after saying he’s confident there will be a 2027 Major League Baseball season, Christopher “Mad Dog” Russo is worried. We’ve known baseball was heading toward a lockout for about as long as we’ve known the current collective bargaining agreement between MLB and the MLB players was set to expire after the 2026 season. Even while knowing a lengthy lockout was looming, Russo confidently predicted there will be a 2027 MLB season this past September. But we haven’t even made it to the lockout yet, and Russo is already changing his tune. In recent weeks, commissioner Rob Manfred has maintained the owners will not compromise on their desire to institute a salary cap. The players, meanwhile, have refused to even entertain a CBA proposal from the owners that includes a salary cap. And with no room for negotiation on the horizon, Russo expressed doubt about baseball being played in 2027 during an appearance on The Dan Patrick Show on Friday morning. ﻿ “The players are not going to engage in these last proposals,” Russo told Patrick. “Because if they do that, then they’re basically telling you that we’ll deal with the salary cap.” Russo noted this is likely heading to court, with the players possibly seeking to file a disclaimer of interest to dissolve the union, allowing them to pursue antitrust lawsuits against the league. “If they win, there’s going to be an appeal. If they lose their appeal, this could take forever,” Russo continued. “I don’t talk to the owners, but I do believe they’re very committed to getting this done.” There is some precedent for PA’s filing a disclaimer of interest. The NBPA did it during the 2011 NBA lockout, dissolving the union on Nov. 14 before quickly reaching a tentative CBA agreement on Nov. 26. But MLB owners and players seem further apart on an agreement with a salary cap on the line. And Russo insists MLB is in a better position to institute a salary cap now than they were during the strike shortened season in 1994, because currently, they’re a league ran by lawyers. “Unlike ’94 with [Bud] Selig, who wasn’t a lawyer, they got good lawyers. Manfred’s a lawyer. He want to Harvard Law School. Dan Halem, his right hand-hand man went to Cornell… they got that buttoned-up. And I think they feel the union can’t win in court, so as a result of that, the union’s going to have to fight that in court, and so, this is going to take forever. But I do believe, the owners are very, very committed to getting this fixed once and for all.” “I believe it needs to be fixed. That’s my opinion. Some people would disagree, but I think this is going to be a very long, drawn out process,” Russo added. “It’s a long way to go. It’s Nov. 20. I think the ’27 season is in jeopardy. I really do. The whole season.” MLB owners are more united than ever

item.title: Chivas' five aims for the end of the Apertura 2026
item.description: Chivas' five aims for the end of the Apertura 2026 Guadalajara will face Cruz Azul on Matchday 17 of the Apertura 2026 with a chance to cap off an impressive regular season. Along with seeking an important win in front of their home fans, the Sacred Flock have five key objectives heading into their final match of the tournament. 1. Chasing the top spot Chivas have a chance to finish at the top of the standings. To do so, they need to beat Cruz Azul and hope América lose or draw their match. 2. Finishing with the best home record in the Apertura 2026 Estadio AKRON has been an important venue for Guadalajara, who will look to finish with the most points at home. So far, they have collected 16 of a possible 24 points, with five wins, one draw and two losses, earning 66.7% of the available points and scoring 15 goals. 3. Securing the best defensive record With just 15 goals conceded, the Sacred Flock have all but secured the best defensive record in the league. Their closest challengers have conceded 20 goals, giving Guadalajara a five-goal advantage in this category. 4. Staying unbeaten away from home Guadalajara will also finish the Apertura 2026 as the only team unbeaten away from home. They recorded three wins and five draws in their eight away matches, a record that reflects their consistency throughout the regular season. 5. Signing off with a win in front of the Red-and-White Nation Finally, Chivas will look to give their fans one last reason to celebrate at Estadio AKRON before the start of the playoffs. Facing a direct rival in the battle at the top of the standings, the Sacred Flock will have the opportunity to close out the regular season with a convincing performance and a win that boosts their ambitions heading into the Liguilla. item.title: Justin Reid pens farewell letter to Saints after release from team
item.description: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Justin Reid pens farewell letter to Saints after release from team appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Veteran safety Justin Reid penned an emotional farewell letter to the New Orleans Saints on Friday following reports that the organization granted his request for a release ahead of its Week 11 matchup against the Chicago Bears. Reid shared a lengthy statement on X, formerly known as Twitter, expressing his appreciation for the organization, teammates and fans after spending nearly two seasons in New Orleans. “I genuinely enjoyed my time here and have nothing but love and respect for this city and the people who make it so special,” Reid wrote. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 29-year-old also thanked Saints owner Gayle Benson, general manager Mickey Loomis and head coach Kellen Moore for giving him an opportunity to represent the franchise. “To my teammates, I love you guys. I’m grateful for the relationships we built and the time we shared. I’ll be rooting hard for each and every one of you,” Reid added. Reid acknowledged that his departure came under circumstances he had not anticipated, although he emphasized that his appreciation for New Orleans remained unchanged. Thank you New Orleans ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/FNHDVM6l1A — Justin Reid (@JustinqReid) November 20, 2026 “In life and in sports, things don’t always go the way you planned or hoped they would. Unfortunately, this is one of those moments,” Reid wrote. “I truly want to see this team and this city thrive. No one deserves it more than New Orleans and the Saints.” Justin Reid’s departure comes amid Saints’ disappointing season Reid signed a three-year, $31.5 million contract with New Orleans in March 2025 after spending three seasons with the Kansas City Chiefs, where he won two Super Bowl championships. The former Stanford standout started all 24 games he played for the Saints, recording 118 tackles, one interception and half a sack. Through nine games this season, Reid registered 46 tackles and two tackles for loss. His departure comes as New Orleans (3-6) attempts to rebound from a disappointing start to the season. The Saints will travel to face the Bears (7-2) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox, with the organization now facing additional questions about its defensive secondary. item.title: 3 potential X-factors on the Bills defense at Dolphins in Week 11
item.description: The Buffalo Bills move forward in the 2026 NFL season with a matchup against the Miami Dolphins at home with a 1 p.m. kickoff on Sunday from Highmark Stadium en route. The Bills defense will play its part, as always. While game plans, coaching, and strategy will play a role, sometimes a big emphasis will sit with some individual players. In terms of the Bills defense, who could those be? Here are Bills Wire's three potential X-factors on the Bills (8-1) defense against the Dolphins (1-8) in Week 11 : CB Davison Igbinosun The Bills have some health question marks in the secondary. Will Christian Benford (wrist) play dinged up? Or will Tre'Davious White get a call up from the practice squad? Regardless, that means the second-round rookie in Igbinosun needs to do his job... and he's been good at that lately. Keep it up. LB Terrel Bernard The Dolphins are rolling with backup quarterback Kyle McCord on Sunday. This selection is easy to see. The goal of the entire Bills defense, will be to make the barely tested McCord beat you. The way to do that is by shutting down the rushing attack and running back Ollie Gordon II. Bernard is going to be a big factor in stopping Miami's ground game. DE Greg Rousseau Rousseau is leading the Bills with eight sacks in 2026. That is potentially bad news for McCord because of right tackle Austin Jackson. The starting tackle for Miami is ranked the second-worst offensive tackle in the NFL by Pro Football Focus right now. Rousseau has a real chance to get to McCord and add to his sack totals in this outing. item.title: Patriots hit with double injury blow to Drake Maye, A.J. Brown
item.description: Patriots hit with double injury blow to Drake Maye, A.J. Brown originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots ' season has not gone as expected, largely due to a slew of injuries to key players. That will continue well into December as the team got a double dose of bad injury news. Quarterback Drake Maye and wide receiver A.J. Brown suffered injuries in Germany against the Lions that forced both players to miss the rest of the 35-10 loss. After further evaluation, both will be out for the foreseeable future, forcing the Patriots to turn elsewhere when they return to the field. Maye's injury occurred in the first quarter on a sack by Aidan Hutchinson, while Brown got injured while the team was already down 25 points. New England is on a bye this week, but both players will not be back when the team returns to action next week. Here's more on Drake Maye's and A.J. Brown's injuries. MORE : Aidan Hutchinson's sack of Drake Maye changes AFC, NFC playoff races Drake Maye injury update On Friday, ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss announced that Drake Maye has a fractured right fibula, which will keep him out for most, if not all, of the regular season. The injury does not require surgery, which increases the possibility that Maye can return this season. Additionally, Maye's injury doesn't include ligament damage, a big reason he isn't undergoing surgery. Aidan Hutchinson's sack on Drake Maye *seemed like a textbook hip drop tackle. *it's been a couple years but I still don't fully know what the league deems a hip drop tackle **a penalty flag would not have made Maye's injury disappear https://t.co/rJN8RITk46 — Michael Hurley (@michaelFhurley) November 15, 2026 While Maye is a candidate for injured reserve, the Patriots are approaching their limit on players they can place on IR, so the quarterback may remain on the active roster for now. This is Maye's first major injury since he took over as the Patriots' starting quarterback in 2024. In Maye's place, Tommy DeVito is expected to get the start for New England next week. MORE : Puka Nacua out months after knee surgery A.J. Brown injury update ESPN also reported that A.J. Brown has a hamstring injury that will keep him out for multiple weeks. That's along with the ankle sprain Brown suffered earlier this year and the knee injury he has been dealing with. Brown has had his share of injuries in his career, but this season has been especially difficult with three separate injuries in the first three months. The veteran has played in just four games this year, and he left two of them after suffering injuries. This the one time AJ Brown actually looked like himself this season and of course he had to get injured on the play. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. Jansen had appeared to hint at questions over how the club addressed some of the shortcomings in terms of player recruitment. In his prematch press conference ahead of the win over D.C. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.) item.title: How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊
item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
